sources.title: Dialetto bolognese (Wikipedia in italiano)
sources.reliability_notes: Uses the Canepari-Vitali OLM spelling; some parts are uncited. Facts only, rephrased.
sources.relevant_sections: Ortografia, articoli, pronomi, plurali, essere/mangiare, numerali, negazione brîṡa
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors

sources.title: Bolognese dialect (Wikipedia, English)
sources.reliability_notes: Detailed grammar sections (clitics, negation, plurals, participles, syntax) with example sentences; the page itself notes some inconsistent tables and missing citations.
sources.relevant_sections: Orthography, subject clitic table, avair/èser, negation, plurals, articles, examples, mò, es
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors

sources.title: English Wiktionary, Emilian (Bolognese) entries: andèr, fèr, vlair, dîr, psair, savair, magnèr, sucèr, brîṡa
sources.reliability_notes: Conjugation tables built from Vitali-Lepri; each verb is a separate page on en.wiktionary.org (andèr, fèr, vlair, dîr, psair, savair, magnèr, sucèr, brîṡa).
sources.relevant_sections: Present indicative paradigms, participles, brîṡa usage and etymology
sources.author: Wiktionary contributors

sources.title: Verbix: Bolognese verb conjugation (conjugation classes)
sources.license: Site terms (free to read); facts only
sources.reliability_notes: Model paradigms for the four conjugation classes (mandèr, parair, adliżer, finîr) incl. imperfect and future.
sources.relevant_sections: Conjugation classes, imperfect, future, gerund, participle
sources.author: Verbix

sources.title: Socc'mel (Wikipedia in italiano)
sources.reliability_notes: Cites Menarini, Lepri-Vitali (2007), Mainoldi, Panzini, Treccani 'Intercalari'. Gives meaning, spelling variants, softening of use.
sources.relevant_sections: Meaning, sucèr link, variants soccia/bän/in pónta, usage, bibliography
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors

sources.title: Al sît bulgnaiṡ: Parôl (lessico), including Menarini's entry on socc'mel and a phrasebook
sources.license: Site content, all rights reserved; facts only
sources.reliability_notes: Maintained by Daniele Vitali's bolognese site. The text as fetched had encoding corruption: diacritics of many items could not be read, so only forms with clear base letters are used and flagged.
sources.relevant_sections: Menarini entry (shibboleth, variants, replies), phrasebook, word list
sources.author: Il Sito Bolognese (D. Vitali et al.)

sources.title: Al sît bulgnaiṡ: Ortografia and Fonetica pages
sources.license: Site content, all rights reserved; facts only
sources.reliability_notes: Describes the OLM spelling (Canepari-Vitali 1995) used by the Lepri-Vitali dictionary. Fetched text had encoding corruption in the vowel table; rules on s/ṡ, z/ż, apostrophes and doubling were legible.
sources.relevant_sections: Accent use, s/ṡ z/ż, apostrophe (apocope marked, aphaeresis not), consonant length
sources.author: Daniele Vitali / Il Sito Bolognese

sources.title: Al sît bulgnaiṡ: Libri (reviews, Dante translation snippets)
sources.license: Site content, all rights reserved; facts only
sources.reliability_notes: Only the first part of the very long page was read; used for two literary lines (a rendering of Dante's 'dove il si suona' as 'dòvv as dìs sèmper sòccmel' and the proverb 'Al pan di èter l é sèt gràsst'). Diacritics possibly altered by encoding.
sources.author: Il Sito Bolognese

sources.title: Proverbi bolognesi (Wikiquote in italiano)
sources.reliability_notes: 12 proverbs with Italian gloss, taken from Coronedi Berti, Vocabolario bolognese italiano (1869-74) and Lepri-Vitali. Spelling is mixed (19th-century and modern), so it is quoted as printed.
sources.author: Wikiquote contributors

sources.title: Socmel! (socmel.it): Dizionarietto bolognese and 'Perché proprio Socmel?'
sources.license: Site content, all rights reserved; facts only
sources.reliability_notes: Popular tourism/culture site; its own footer says texts were written with AI assistance and reviewed. Spellings are modern OLM-like (Bulåggna, Brîṡa, tajadèl). Used only for headwords and short glosses, treated as unverified unless confirmed elsewhere.
sources.relevant_sections: 36-entry dizionarietto; discussion of the spelling 'Socmel'/'sòccmel' and tones of use
sources.author: Socmel! project

sources.title: Slengo: socmel
sources.relevant_sections: Definition 'intercalare bolognese buono per ogni occasione'
sources.author: Slengo users

sources.title: Succede solo a Bologna: guide to feeling at home in Bologna
sources.license: Site content, all rights reserved; facts only
sources.reliability_notes: Popular blog. Its items (fare balotta, bòna lé, bella vèz, bandéssa, ói...) are Bologna-flavoured colloquialisms, many of them in Bolognese Italian rather than dialect proper.
sources.author: Succede solo a Bologna

sources.title: Treccani Vocabolario: sbolognare
sources.reliability_notes: Used only to document that sbolognare is Italian of Bolognese-furbesco origin.
sources.author: Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana

sources.title: Socc'mel ban, raccolta di proverbi bolognesi (F. Riggillo, ill. G. Ravazzini, 2024), bookseller listing
sources.reliability_notes: Only a bookseller listing was read. It documents that 'Soccmel' is used as a title word in a Bolognese-proverb book; the book itself was not read.
sources.author: Edizioni Artestampa

sources.license: Site content, all rights reserved; facts only
